Tessa / team —

Attached is the sketch and the KMS diagram (private-dedicated-vpc-sketch.pdf, kms-integration-diagram.svg). Quick technical summary / talking points for the call:

1) Topology summary- Customer workloads run in the customer-managed VPC (customer-owned CIDR). The Redwood Private control plane components run in a customer-dedicated account/region and communicate over a VPC peer (or IPsec for on-prem). There is no hairpinning through Redwood public tenants.

2) Isolation controls- Control plane is logically separated from data plane; management traffic flows over a dedicated peering link. Network ACLs and security groups enforce strict port-level allow lists. We do not place customer data on shared storage in the control plane; KV caches are ephemeral and encrypted.

3) Egress and ingress- All outbound egress from compute in the customer VPC uses the customer's NAT Gateway (or configured egress gateway/Transit Gateway). We can optionally route telemetry/audit exports to a dedicated S3 bucket in the customer's account (recommended for regulatory customers).

4) KMS / key ownership- Customer-managed keys supported via AWS KMS with cross-account grants; for HSM-backed keys we integrate with customer HSM using an approved connector (we provide an HSM proxy pattern). Private control plane only stores key references; ciphertext never stored in plaintext.

5) Audit log handling- Control plane emits structured audit events to CloudWatch/Stackdriver and optionally to a customer-owned S3 bucket or SIEM via secure forwarder. Retention policy defaults to 90 days; we can extend to customer required retention windows and provide exports for SOC 2 evidence.

6) Access and bastioning- No permanent inbound SSH to control-plane hosts. Admin access via ephemeral bastion (short-lived certificates) and role-based access controls with MFA enforced.

7) Evidence bundle- I've started the evidence index (sig_evidence_index.csv) with references to config screenshots (IAM role policies, VPC peering config), architecture diagram PDFs, and a sample retention configuration. We will mark items that require customer-signed NDA before sharing full diagrams.

Notes on redaction: Public diagram will show logical components and peering arrows only. Full diagrams have subnet/CIDR and peering IDs and will be provided via secure share if ACME signs the NDA or during an auditor workshop.
